failures.observed: The second development command failed and appended wf083_infrastructure__development_load_002 because rolling.cpython-312-darwin.so could not locate @rpath/libc++.1.dylib; the embedded failed path was /opt/anaconda3/lib.
failures.root_cause: The existing compiled Qlib rolling extension was built for the local Conda runtime layout, while the isolated runtime has no libc++.1.dylib in its own lib directory.
failures.correction: Do not rewrite the extension or bypass the failure. Evaluate frozen interpreter-only compatibility alternatives before another retry.

failures.observed: The local Conda Python successfully imported qlib.data with numpy 1.26.4, pandas 2.2.2, pyarrow 16.1.0, and scipy 1.13.1, but its global pip check exited nonzero for unrelated streamlit/protobuf and python-jose/pyasn1 constraints.
failures.root_cause: The broad Conda environment has two dependency metadata conflicts outside the Campaign083 development import and calculation path.
failures.correction: If the Conda interpreter is later authorized, bind its executable and libc++ hashes, record the two unrelated pip-check conflicts explicitly, and require the exact Campaign083 imports/tests rather than claim a globally clean environment.

failures.observed: DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH pointed at the Conda lib directory and caused isolated-runtime NumPy 2.3.5 to resolve an incompatible BLAS/Accelerate symbol before qlib.data import.
failures.root_cause: DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH globally overrides native dependency resolution and is too broad for a one-library repair.
failures.correction: Reject DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH for development; never use this diagnostic environment for a trial.

failures.observed: DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH located libc++, but the rolling extension then failed because it was compiled against NumPy 1.x and cannot run with isolated-runtime NumPy 2.3.5.
failures.root_cause: The compiled extension ABI requires a NumPy 1.x development interpreter, not only a dynamic-library path fallback.
failures.correction: Reject the isolated NumPy 2.x interpreter for Qlib development. Use only a separately frozen NumPy 1.x-compatible interpreter if all campaign bindings and repair-state tests pass.
